- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp declines or spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends — model reacts slower than actual market action.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when historical mean is high (e.g., 2024-02-06), suggesting underweighting of recent volatility or overconfidence in downward trends.
- When true price spikes occur, model often overshoots the peak and then underestimates the subsequent correction — especially in 30-day forecasts.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to anticipate or adjust for price returning to historical averages after sharp moves.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture short-term volatility or sudden reversals, especially in the middle of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits “late correction” bias — corrects only after the true value has already moved significantly, leading to persistent lag in the final 10–15 days.
